# Preschool and daycare fees in Gurgaon: what parents actually pay
URL: https://www.kribblecare.com/blog/preschool-fees-gurgaon/

Preschool fees in Gurgaon range from about ₹16,000 to ₹2 lakh a year, with a median of about ₹55,400, based on [Kiddenz's Gurgaon listings](https://kiddenz.com/gurugram). Where you live changes the number a lot. On top of the yearly fee, expect one-time charges such as admission, which can add thousands more in the first year.

## The citywide picture

Kiddenz lists 567 verified preschools and daycares in Gurgaon (officially Gurugram). Across those listings:

- **Median annual fee:** about ₹55,400
- **Lowest:** roughly ₹16,000 a year
- **Highest:** roughly ₹2 lakh a year

The median means half the listed centres charge less and half charge more. It's a better guide than an average, which a few very expensive centres can pull up.

These figures mix preschools and daycares, and listings change. Use them to set expectations, not to judge a single centre's quote.

## Fees by area

Location is one of the biggest drivers of price. Kiddenz's sector pages show the spread clearly:

| Area | Median annual fee (Kiddenz) |
|---|---|
| [Sector 51](https://kiddenz.com/gurugram/sector-51) | about ₹1.1 lakh |
| Sector 30 | about ₹72,800 |
| Citywide median | about ₹55,400 |
| Sector 92 | about ₹32,400 |

A family in Sector 51 might see a typical fee more than three times higher than a family in Sector 92. Our area guides go into more detail, starting with [Sectors 45 to 51](/blog/daycare-sector-45-51-gurgaon/) and Dwarka Expressway and New Gurgaon.

## Premium and budget examples

Two real examples show the gap.

At the premium end, the [Kiddenz page for Klay](https://kiddenz.com/brand/klay) shows annual fees of about ₹1.49 to 1.95 lakh. There's a one-time admission fee of about ₹28,000.

At the budget end, a franchise preschool in Sector 41 listed on SchoolsUniverse charges about ₹35,000 a year. Its admission fee is about ₹5,000.

Neither price tells you about quality on its own. A higher fee may pay for longer hours, meals, bigger spaces or a lower ratio. A lower fee may simply reflect lower rent. You only find out by visiting.

## What drives the price

When two centres quote very different fees, it's usually down to a few things:

- **Rent and location.** Space usually costs more on main roads and in high-end sectors.
- **Hours.** A full-day daycare costs more than a three-hour preschool session.
- **Ratio and staffing.** More adults per child means a higher wage bill.
- **Meals.** Cooked meals on site add cost, and some centres charge separately.
- **Space and facilities.** Outdoor play areas, activity rooms and air-conditioning all cost money.
- **Brand.** Chains and franchises may charge for their curriculum and materials.

Ask each centre what the fee covers. A good answer lists it plainly: "Fees include snacks and lunch, materials and the daily updates. Transport and after-hours care are extra."

## The one-time and hidden costs

The yearly fee is rarely the whole story. Ask about each of these:

| Charge | What to ask |
|---|---|
| Admission fee | Is it one-time? Is any of it refundable? |
| Registration fee | Is it adjusted against fees if you enrol? |
| Security deposit | When and how is it returned? |
| Annual or development charge | Is it charged every year? |
| Meals | Included, or charged monthly? |
| Transport | Per month or per term? Fixed or by distance? |
| Late pickup | Per minute, per hour or per incident? |
| Activities and events | Are there extra charges for trips, costumes or classes? |
| Uniform and books | Bought from the centre, or anywhere? |

Our full [daycare fees explainer](/blog/daycare-fees-explained/) covers each one, including refund terms.

## How to budget for the first year

Work out the true first-year cost for each centre on your shortlist. It's simple:

1. Take the annual fee (or monthly fee × 12).
2. Add every one-time charge: admission, registration, deposit.
3. Add meals, transport and any late-pickup hours you'll realistically need.
4. Add a small buffer for events and supplies.

Then compare totals, not monthly fees. A centre with a lower monthly fee but a large admission fee can cost more in year one.

Remember the second year too. Ask whether fees rise each year and by how much. Ask what you'd pay if you moved from half-day to full-day.

## Fee isn't everything

It's easy to let price lead. Try to keep it as one factor among several. Safety, staff, ratio and your child's happiness matter more over a full year.

Our [complete checklist for choosing a daycare](/blog/how-to-choose-a-daycare/) and the [side-by-side scorecard](/blog/compare-daycares-scorecard/) help you weigh fees against everything else. For more on the local picture, see our [guide to daycare in Gurgaon](/blog/daycare-in-gurgaon-guide/).

When Kribble launches, you'll be able to see admission, registration, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and annual plans side by side for each listed centre.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the average preschool fee in Gurgaon?

Kiddenz's Gurgaon listings show a median annual fee of about ₹55,400. The range runs from roughly ₹16,000 to ₹2 lakh a year. Your area, the hours you need and what's included will move the number a lot.

### Why are fees in some sectors so much higher?

Rent is likely part of it, since space costs more in high-end sectors. Centres there may also offer longer hours or more facilities. On Kiddenz, Sector 51's median is about ₹1.1 lakh, while Sector 92's is about ₹32,400.

### Is the admission fee refundable?

It depends on the centre, and many admission fees are not. Ask before you pay, and get the answer in writing. Registration fees and security deposits often have different rules, so ask about each.

### Should I pay preschool fees yearly or monthly?

Yearly can be cheaper if there's a discount, but it's harder to leave. Monthly or quarterly gives you flexibility in the first year while you see how your child settles. Check the refund policy either way.


---

# Daycare safety checklist: 20 things to check before you enrol
URL: https://www.kribblecare.com/blog/daycare-safety-checklist/

A good daycare safety checklist covers five things: the people, the building, pickup, emergencies and everyday hygiene. Check all five in person before you enrol. Glossy brochures and a friendly owner are not enough.

Take the 20 points below on your visit. For the wider picture beyond safety, start with our [complete guide to choosing a daycare](/blog/how-to-choose-a-daycare/).

## The people

Staff matter most. A safe building with careless adults is not a safe daycare.

1. **Background checks for every adult.** Ask whether all staff have police verification. That includes teachers, helpers, cooks, drivers and guards. A good answer: "Yes, for everyone, before they start. We keep the records on file."
2. **A written child protection policy.** Ask to see it. It should say how staff behave with children, who changes nappies and how concerns are reported.
3. **Child protection awareness.** Ask how staff are trained on it. Under India's [POCSO Act, 2012](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/14753/1/pocso.pdf), anyone who knows of or suspects a sexual offence against a child must report it to the police. The person in charge of an institution can be punished for not reporting. A centre should know this and have a clear reporting process.
4. **Two-adult rules.** Ask whether a child is ever alone with one adult behind a closed door. Careful centres keep doors open, or use glass panels, where children are changed.
5. **Enough adults per child.** Count the adults and children in each room yourself. Our [teacher-to-child ratio guide](/blog/teacher-child-ratio-guide/) explains what to look for by age.
6. **Low staff turnover.** Ask how long the lead teachers have worked there. Familiar adults notice when something is off with a child.

## The building

7. **Secure entry.** The main door should be locked or guarded. Strangers should not be able to walk in. Notice whether anyone asks who you are.
8. **Safe stairs, windows and balconies.** Look for gates on stairs, grilles or locks on windows and high railings on balconies or terraces.
9. **Covered sockets and hidden wires.** Get down to your child's eye level. Check for open sockets, loose wires, sharp corners and heavy furniture that could tip.
10. **Medicines and cleaners out of reach.** These should be in locked or high cupboards. Not on a shelf in the bathroom.
11. **Fire safety.** Look for working extinguishers, a clear exit route and a second way out. Ask when they last ran a fire drill with the children.
12. **Safe outdoor play area.** Check the boundary wall or fence, the play equipment and the surface beneath it. Ask how often equipment is checked.

## Pickup and drop

13. **Authorised pickup list.** Only named adults should be able to collect your child. Ask what happens if someone new turns up. A good answer: "We call you first and check their ID."
14. **Sign-in and sign-out.** There should be a record of when each child arrives and leaves, and who brought or collected them.
15. **Transport checks.** If the centre runs a van, ask whether a female attendant travels on it. Ask about seat belts and the driver's verification.

## Emergencies and health

16. **First aid training and a kit.** Ask who is trained in paediatric first aid and when. Ask to see the kit, and check that it is stocked.
17. **A clear sick and incident policy.** Ask what happens if your child falls, gets a fever or has an allergic reaction. They should call you, write it down and share an incident report.
18. **Allergy and medicine records.** Ask how they record allergies and how staff know which child has one. Ask who gives medicines and whether they need your written consent.

## Everyday hygiene

19. **Clean nappy and toilet areas.** Look for a separate changing area, handwashing right after, and child-sized toilets that are actually clean.
20. **Safe food and water.** Ask where food is cooked, who cooks it and how drinking water is purified. Look into the kitchen if you can.

## What about CCTV?

CCTV can help, but it is not on this list as a must. Cameras record what happens. They don't prevent it. Good staff, good policies and alert adults do that. Read [what CCTV in a daycare can and can't tell you](/blog/cctv-in-daycare/) before you treat it as a deciding factor.

## How to use this checklist

You won't get perfect answers to all 20. What matters is how the centre responds.

| Response | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| Clear answer, shows you a record or document | Strong sign. They've thought about it. |
| "We're working on it" with a date | Fair. Follow up before enrolling. |
| Vague, defensive or annoyed | Concern. Safety questions should be welcome. |
| "Nobody has ever asked that" | Ask yourself why. |

If a point worries you, check our list of [daycare red flags](/blog/daycare-red-flags/) for what to do next. Visit twice if you can, once at drop-off time and once mid-day. A [trial day](/blog/trial-day-before-enrolling/) shows you more than any tour.

Kribble's team will physically visit and check every centre before it is listed. You'll be able to see safety details alongside fees and photos, but still visit yourself.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the most important thing on a daycare safety checklist?

The people. Background checks, a written child protection policy and enough adults per child matter more than any camera or gadget.

### Should daycare staff have police verification?

It is a sensible thing to ask for, for every adult who works there. That includes helpers, cooks, guards and drivers, not just teachers. Ask whether the centre keeps the records on file.

### What does POCSO mean for a daycare?

The POCSO Act, 2012 is India's law on sexual offences against children. It requires anyone who knows of or suspects such an offence to report it to the police. A daycare should have a clear reporting process and staff who know it.

### Is a daycare with CCTV safer?

Not automatically. CCTV records what happens but doesn't stop it. Staff quality, supervision and policies matter more, so treat CCTV as one point among many.


---

# Going back to work after maternity leave: a childcare plan that works
URL: https://www.kribblecare.com/blog/childcare-after-maternity-leave/

Start looking for childcare about three months before you go back to work. Plan two to four weeks of settling in before your first full day. Then build a backup plan, because the first sick day arrives sooner than you expect.

Going back is a big shift for the whole family. A clear plan makes it far less stressful.

## Know your leave and workplace rights first

Your timeline starts with your leave. Under India's [Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017](https://www.labour.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/1a64517bcba2fab5650a9ff66d429080.pdf), eligible women get up to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for their first two children. It added a creche requirement for establishments with 50 or more employees. It also let employers allow work from home after leave, by mutual agreement.

Since 21 November 2025, these provisions sit within the [Code on Social Security, 2020](https://www.pib.gov.in/FactsheetDetails.aspx?id=150473). It keeps the creche rule for establishments with 50 or more employees. Check with HR how your employer applies it. Our guide to [creches at work in India](/blog/creche-at-work-india/) explains how to ask.

## A timeline that works

| When | What to do |
|---|---|
| 3 months before return | Decide on the type of care. Shortlist 4 to 6 options. Check HR for a creche or tie-up. |
| 10 to 8 weeks before | Visit your top 2 or 3. Ask about fees, timings and infant care. |
| 6 to 4 weeks before | Enrol and pay. Fill in forms with both parents' details. Plan your backup. |
| 4 to 2 weeks before | Start settling in: short visits, then half days. |
| Final week | A full day or two while you're still home. Practise the morning routine. |
| First weeks back | Expect a few sick days. Keep the backup plan ready. |

Infant rooms fill up, so don't leave it late.

## Daycare, nanny or family?

It depends on your child's age, your hours, your budget and who's around you.

| | Daycare or creche | Nanny at home | Grandparents or family |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best for | Predictable office hours | Long or irregular hours | Close-by family who want to help |
| Strengths | Trained staff, routine, other children | One-to-one care, no commute for baby | Trust, love, flexibility |
| Watch out for | Fixed timings, more early illnesses | Single point of failure, harder to supervise | Fatigue, different parenting styles |
| Backup needed for | Centre closures, child's sick days | Nanny's leave and sick days | Family travel and health |

Many families mix these, such as daycare with a grandparent covering sick days. If you're weighing a daycare or a preschool for an older sibling, our guide to [preschool vs daycare](/blog/preschool-vs-daycare/) helps.

## Choosing a daycare for a young baby

Infant care needs extra checks. On your visit, ask:

- What is the youngest age you take, and how many babies are in the infant room?
- How many adults care for the babies at any time?
- How do you handle expressed milk or formula? How is it stored and labelled?
- Can I visit to feed during the day?
- How do you record feeds, naps and nappies? (See what daily updates to expect.)
- Where do babies sleep, and who checks on them?

For the full process, use our checklist on [how to choose a daycare](/blog/how-to-choose-a-daycare/). Check ratios carefully, as babies need more adults per child. Our [teacher-to-child ratio guide](/blog/teacher-child-ratio-guide/) explains why.

## Plan the settling-in weeks

Don't make your first day at work your child's first full day at daycare. Most children need time to adjust.

A gentle plan:

1. **Week one:** an hour or two with you nearby, then short stays without you.
2. **Week two:** half days, including one meal and one nap.
3. **Week three:** full days, ideally while you're still at home and can pick up early.

Some children settle in days. Others take a few weeks. Read our guide to [settling into daycare](/blog/settling-in-at-daycare/) for goodbye routines and what's normal.

## Build the backup plan now

Your child will catch colds in the first months of group care. Centres also close for holidays. Plan for this before you need it.

- **Agree who takes sick days.** Split them between both parents, not one by default. Our piece on [dads and daycare](/blog/dads-and-daycare/) has practical ideas.
- **Line up one or two backups.** A family member, a trusted neighbour, or a centre that offers single days.
- **Talk to your manager early.** Ask about flexible hours or work from home for the first few weeks.

See [backup childcare options](/blog/backup-childcare-one-day/) for more.

## Look after yourself too

The first weeks back are tiring. You may feel guilty, relieved or both. That's common. Keep the routine simple, share the load, and give it a month.

Kribble will let you compare verified daycares in Gurugram by fees, timings and availability, and book One-Day Daycare when your usual plan falls through.

## Frequently asked questions

### When should I start looking for daycare before going back to work?

About three months before your return date is a good start. That gives you time to visit, enrol, and settle your child in over two to four weeks before your first full day back.

### How long is maternity leave in India?

Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, eligible women get up to 26 weeks of paid leave for their first two children. These provisions now sit within the Code on Social Security, 2020. Check with HR how it applies to you.

### Does my employer have to provide a creche?

Establishments with 50 or more employees are required to provide a creche facility, either their own or a shared one. Ask HR how your employer meets this. Our guide to creches at work explains how to raise it.

### Is a daycare or a nanny better after maternity leave?

Neither is better for everyone. Daycare suits predictable hours and offers routine and trained staff. A nanny suits long or irregular hours. Many families combine one with family support for sick days.

# What is Kribble? Verified childcare, from one day to every day
URL: https://www.kribblecare.com/blog/what-is-kribble/

Kribble is a childcare discovery and booking app for parents in India, starting in Gurgaon. Our team visits and checks every daycare, preschool and playschool before it appears in the app. Once it launches, you'll be able to compare centres and book anything from a single day to a full year. You'll also pay fees and get teacher updates in one place.

Kribble is not live yet. Right now, you can join the waitlist.

## The problem we're trying to fix

Finding childcare usually means a patchwork of WhatsApp groups, Google searches and weekend visits. Fees are hard to compare. Photos online may be years old. And it is hard to know what a centre is really like until you are standing inside it.

We estimate there are about 850 private preschools and daycares in Gurgaon alone. That is a lot of choice, and a lot of legwork for a parent with a job and a toddler.

Kribble is our attempt to make that search shorter and clearer, without pretending it can replace your own judgement.

## How Kribble will work

### 1. Every centre is visited first

Every centre listed on Kribble is physically visited and checked by the Kribble team before it appears in the app. The visit covers safety, staff credentials, hygiene, ratios and facilities, and our team photographs the space itself, so the photos you see are the real rooms.

Verification is a starting point, not a guarantee. Our guide on [what a "verified" daycare actually means](/blog/what-verified-daycare-means/) explains what it can and cannot tell you.

### 2. Compare centres side by side

You'll be able to compare centres on:

- Location, timings and availability
- Approach and facilities
- Real photos and safety details
- Fees, with admission, registration, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and annual plans shown side by side

Seeing the plans together makes hidden costs easier to spot. Our explainer on [daycare and preschool fees](/blog/daycare-fees-explained/) covers what each charge usually means.

### 3. Book the care you need

Kribble will cover the early years, from a baby's first daycare to primary school. You'll be able to book:

| Plan | What it's for |
|---|---|
| Preschool admissions | Enrolling for the school year |
| Monthly daycare | Regular full-day care for working parents |
| Half-day daycare | Mornings or afternoons only |
| After-school care | Care after preschool or primary school |
| Holiday camps | School breaks |
| One-Day Daycare | Verified childcare booked for a single day |

One-Day Daycare is useful when your nanny cancels, or when you want to [try a daycare for a day before you enrol](/blog/trial-day-before-enrolling/). Our guide to [backup childcare](/blog/backup-childcare-one-day/) covers other options too.

### 4. Enquire, enrol and pay in one place

You'll be able to send enquiries, enrol and pay fees securely in the app, with receipts and reminders. Partner centres will offer member discounts on enrolment fees, activity packs and monthly plans.

### 5. Stay in touch with your child's day

Photos, updates and notes from teachers will arrive in one feed, instead of scattered across messages and calls.

## What's coming later

- **Caregivers at home.** On-demand caregivers at home are part of the plan, alongside centres.
- **More cities.** Kribble launches in Gurugram first. Other cities will follow, with no dates yet.
- **A profile of your child's early years.** Later, we plan a longitudinal profile combining teacher notes, milestone tracking and AI insights. This will not be available at launch.

## What Kribble is not

We would rather be clear about our limits now than disappoint you later.

- **It is not live yet.** You cannot book or pay through Kribble today.
- **It is Gurgaon only at launch.** If you live elsewhere, join the waitlist and we'll tell you when we reach your city.
- **Verification is not a licence.** It means our team has visited and checked the centre. It is not a government licence, and it is not a guarantee of safety.
- **It does not replace your visit.** Please still see a centre in person and ask your own questions. Our [daycare checklist](/blog/how-to-choose-a-daycare/) can help.

## Who is building Kribble

Kribble is built by Little Orbit Technology Private Limited. The founders are:

- **Piyush Chawla**, Co-founder and CEO, who leads vision, operations and centre partnerships.
- **Ketan Pandey**, Co-founder and CTO, who leads technology and product.
- **Anand Singh**, Co-founder and CMO, who leads growth, brand and market expansion.

You can reach the team at team@kribblecare.com.

## Where to start

While you wait, our [guide to daycare in Gurgaon](/blog/daycare-in-gurgaon-guide/) covers areas, typical fees and what to check. If you run a centre, read how Kribble's partner programme works.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Kribble free for parents?

Yes. Searching, comparing and shortlisting verified centres is free. You only ever pay the centre's own fees, and members get discounts at partner centres.

### When will Kribble launch?

Kribble is pre-launch and will open in Gurgaon first. We have not announced a date yet. Join the waitlist at kribblecare.com to hear as soon as it goes live.

### What does "verified" mean on Kribble?

Every centre on Kribble is physically visited and checked by the Kribble team before it is listed. It is not a government licence or a safety guarantee. You should still visit the centre yourself before you enrol.

### Is Kribble available outside Gurgaon?

Not at launch. Kribble starts in Gurgaon, and other cities are planned, but there are no dates yet. You can join the waitlist from anywhere to hear when it reaches you.

### I run a daycare. How do I get listed?

Kribble has a partner programme for centres. Every centre is visited and checked before it is listed. You can contact the team through "Partner With Us" or "Schedule a Demo" at kribblecare.com.
